facts.raw_span: a 2-year history of swelling of her right upper eyelid
which had discharged pus for the previous 10 months
without any trauma to her head
She denied any symptoms, including fever
headache, or nasal discharge
an immovable scarlike node, 11 × 7 mm, on her right upper eyelid discharging pus
High signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
without any abnormal lesions in the orbital or intracranial tissue
Opacification on right frontal sinus, right ethmoid sinus, and right maxillary sinus
expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus without any bone destruction
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, few eosinophils and no sign of malignancy

concepts.why: High signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus, along with opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, suggest chronic frontal sinusitis.
Opacification and expansion of the right ethmoid sinus, along with high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement, suggest chronic ethmoid sinusitis.
Opacification of the right maxillary sinus, along with high signal on T2-weighted image, suggests chronic maxillary sinusitis.
A 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid, with discharge of pus and an immovable scarlike node, suggests preseptal cellulitis.
Discharge of pus from the right upper eyelid, along with an immovable scarlike node, could suggest an orbital abscess.
Mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, along with discharge of pus, suggests a subperiosteal abscess.
A 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid, with discharge of pus, could suggest chronic dacryocystitis.
A 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid, with discharge of pus and an immovable scarlike node, could suggest idiopathic orbital inflammation.

rationales.F01: Swelling of the right upper eyelid could be related to sinusitis or orbital inflammation
rationales.F02: Pus discharge from the eyelid suggests an infectious or inflammatory process
rationales.F06: Immovable scarlike node on the eyelid discharging pus is highly suggestive of preseptal cellulitis or orbital abscess
rationales.F07: Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI is highly suggestive of chronic frontal sinusitis
rationales.F09: Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT is highly suggestive of chronic sinusitis
rationales.F10: Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses without bone destruction is consistent with chronic sinusitis
